actual_copy: New Testament — Matthew 1:1–17, in the text’s order. Verse 1 calls Jesus Christ the son of David, the son of Abraham. Each arrow connects the main-line names using Matthew’s “begat” wording; parentheses give side branches or qualifications, not additional chain links. This follows the text’s wording, without claiming that no generation is omitted: Abraham → Isaac → Jacob → Judas (his brethren are also named) → Phares (Zara is also named; both are of Thamar) → Esrom → Aram → Aminadab → Naasson → Salmon → Booz (of Rachab) → Obed (of Ruth) → Jesse → David (the king) → Solomon (of her that had been the wife of Urias) → Roboam → Abia → Asa → Josaphat → Joram → Ozias → Joatham → Achaz → Ezekias → Manasses → Amon → Josias → Jechonias (his brethren are also named, about the carrying away to Babylon) → Salathiel → Zorobabel → Abiud → Eliakim → Azor → Sadoc → Achim → Eliud → Eleazar → Matthan → Jacob → Joseph. Verse 16 changes the wording: Joseph is “the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ”; the text does not say that Joseph begat Jesus. Verse 17 counts fourteen generations from Abraham to David, fourteen from David to the carrying away into Babylon, and fourteen from then to Christ; no names are added to fit those groups. A repeated name is listed at each place it occurs: Jacob ×2.

actual_copy: New Testament — Luke 3:23–38, in Luke’s order and spelling. Jesus was “about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli.” From Heli on, each name is called the son of the one after it: Heli → Matthat → Levi → Melchi → Janna → Joseph → Mattathias → Amos → Naum → Esli → Nagge → Maath → Mattathias → Semei → Joseph → Juda → Joanna → Rhesa → Zorobabel → Salathiel → Neri → Melchi → Addi → Cosam → Elmodam → Er → Jose → Eliezer → Jorim → Matthat → Levi → Simeon → Juda → Joseph → Jonan → Eliakim → Melea → Menan → Mattatha → Nathan → David → Jesse → Obed → Booz → Salmon → Naasson → Aminadab → Aram → Esrom → Phares → Juda → Jacob → Isaac → Abraham → Thara → Nachor → Saruch → Ragau → Phalec → Heber → Sala → Cainan → Arphaxad → Sem → Noe → Lamech → Mathusala → Enoch → Jared → Maleleel → Cainan → Enos → Seth → Adam, “which was the son of God.” That last link is Luke’s statement, not an ordinary line of descent. A repeated name is listed at each place it occurs (Joseph ×4, Matthat ×2, Levi ×2, Melchi ×2, Mattathias ×2, Juda ×3, Cainan ×2), and the list is not harmonized with Matthew’s.

New Testament — Matthew 21: two sons answer their father’s request differently; then vineyard tenants reject the owner’s servants and kill his son. These are separate parables, not mapped estates or additional historical killings.

New Testament — Mark 12: vineyard tenants mistreat the owner’s servants and kill his beloved son. Mark places the killing before the son is cast out; each Gospel’s order is kept as written, not harmonized.
New Testament — Luke 8: the sower and its interpretation, in terms of hearing and keeping God’s word. This teaching is separate from the chapter’s crossing and healings; no farm is located.

New Testament — Luke 20: vineyard tenants reject the owner’s servants, cast out his beloved son and kill him; the hearers answer “God forbid.” Luke’s sequence is kept as written; the story is not a mapped event.
